A cybersecurity regulator has stated that tech giants need to step up their efforts to combat sextortion, specifically naming companies like Apple, Meta, and Google as needing to do better.

Victims of sextortion are often younger, including children under the age of 16…

A typical sextortion attack involves the perpetrator posing as someone of a similar age to the victim and flirting with them online. At some point, the attacker claims to send an explicit photo of themselves and encourages the victim to reciprocate.

If the victim does send a photo back, the attacker then threatens to make it public and typically claims they will use social media to send copies to the victim's family and friends unless they are paid to delete it.

TNW reported that Australia's cybersecurity regulator, eSafety, stated that tech giants are not doing enough to detect these types of attacks.

Taking Apple as an example, the regulator pointed out that Apple should detect these scam messages sent via iMessage, similar to what is currently done to detect explicit photos being sent to children. The report also noted that Apple needs to make it easier for victims to report such attacks.

The regulator said the scale of the problem is huge, with more than 10% of 16- to 18-year-olds having been affected—over half of whom said the incident occurred before the age of 16.

9to5Mac's take

The scale of the problem appears to be quite severe, and there have already been cases of teenagers committing suicide as a result of sextortion. I agree with the regulator's view that tech giants, including Apple, should strengthen their efforts to combat these crimes.

iMessage communications use end-to-end encryption. However, Apple's existing explicit image detection features have proven that the company can perform on-device analysis on the recipient's device without compromising privacy. A similar approach could be used to detect these scam messages.

Apple may already be working on this issue. Developers have already discovered a malicious message detection feature in iOS 26.6 beta 5.
